identity.realm: No ladder at all, and the absence is the species' rather than hers. The mineral bloom that replaced a lanternfolk's fungal colony holds qi where the colony transacted with it, so nothing in this body is constrained by a structure she does not have: there is no structural gate to fail and therefore no ordinal to quote. She has never been able to say which rung she is on, because her subspecies has never had rungs, and the whole of her practice is spent on a discipline the ladder does not price.

appearance.presentation: A deadlight of the deep quarries, which is a cave body that cannot leave the caves: a lanternfolk shape with a silicate lattice where the luminous hyphae were, and the only member of her subspecies in the registry's service. Her species gained the mind path by dying, and she is the body that makes the receipt legible, which is why nobody has ever asked her whether she can survive leaving the rock.
appearance.age: Fifty-eight, on a subspecies lifespan of about ninety years where the parent line runs to two hundred and fifty, and she is one of the last of her clutch rather than a rarity. The ninety figure is the whole of her species' inheritance and she can state it exactly, the way other people state a name.
appearance.build: Lanternfolk-framed and lighter than her parents were, because the lattice is mineral and does not carry the weight tissue does. Broad through a narrow chest, long in the forearm from a life at stone faces, and cold to the touch in a way that has stopped being remarked on.
appearance.complexion: Grey, faintly translucent at the temple, and lit from within by nothing at all. Her parents' subspecies glows not at all, which is the single most-cited difference between the two and the reason the subspecies is named for what replaced the colony rather than for what it lost.
appearance.hair: Colourless and brittle, cut close at the nape for the dust and re-cut by her own hand. It grows back slowly, because nothing in this body is being repaired, and she has stopped commenting on that.
appearance.eyes: Ordinary human vision, and the only sense that is not worse than her parents'. They see in the dark, unlike the colony that lit a lanternfolk from the inside, and in a quarry that is the difference between a working body and a liability.
appearance.palette: Quarry grey and wet-stone black with one warm value, lamp-ochre, that belongs to the lamps and not to her. She is the least luminous thing on any floor she stands on, which her parents' subspecies would have found unbearable and she finds merely efficient.
appearance.attire: Quarry leather over a felted underlayer, sleeves cut above the wrist so the hands stay bare, and a short apron that has been re-oiled so often it has stopped being leather in three places. She works in the open and refuses to be led underground without the lamp being carried ahead.
appearance.marks: A spread of healed stone dust in the creases of both hands, and a single scar across the outside of the left wrist from the year the floor came in on the intake. She has the scar because a bloom renews nothing, so the record of an injury is permanent and there is no version of her hand that does not carry it.
appearance.bearing: Level, unhurried, and deliberately unlit about it. She stands square in front of a reader and gives them her whole attention, which is a courtesy her subspecies did not inherit and has to be taught, and which she teaches to every junior who joins the intake.

canon.role_in_story: The Field Registry keeps the burnt list, and at a settlement funeral the dead are read as the frame said, not as the funeral said. Every other body in the setting carries a fossil of what it was before it was this, and the frame reads that fossil: a split vessel, a taproot, a second set of shoulders. A deadlight carries no fossil, because what replaced the colony was inert and left nothing behind. Vesna Quill is the reader who has to say so out loud, at funerals, to families, on the record, for ninety years a reading that is true and says nothing about the person in front of her. She does it because her own frame is the control and there is no second deadlight on the plains to check her against, and because the discipline she was raised into is called Void Refinement, which empties a sea of everything in it that was not understood, and she has never once found anything in herself worth keeping that she could not name.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing at the intake bench with her sleeves cut above the wrist and one bare hand flat on a slab, telling a widower that the frame had nothing to give them about his wife and that she was going to keep saying so in the same words until the record was closed.
canon.lore:
A lanternfolk is a body that has outsourced its nervous system to a colony of luminous hyphae threaded through the dermis and into the spinal cord. Human tissue is the substrate and the colony is the organ; neither can be removed from the other and survive. That is why they are still alive at two hundred and fifty years, and it is why they cannot take the mind path at all: the colony answers before the question is finished, so there is no unmediated interior left to cultivate.

Her subspecies is what happened when a colony strain failed and the wound was colonised by something mineral that could survive the same conditions. A silicate lattice grew in place of the hyphae. The body grew around it rather than recovering. What the subspecies gained is the mind path, because nothing in it answers introspection any more, and what it lost is three quarters of its life, because a bloom renews nothing and so nothing in that body is being repaired. Ninety years instead of two hundred and fifty. Ordinary human vision, which in a cavern is the difference between working and being carried. Ordinary human fertility and a gestation four times the parent's rate, which is the only way the caverns have found to keep a lanternfolk-shaped body in them at all.

What her subspecies has is not a ceiling and not a floor. There is no structural gate in her body to fail, because the bloom holds qi where the colony transacted with it, and holding and transacting are different arrangements of the same material. So she cannot quote an ordinal. Not one. She has been asked for one at every reading for nineteen years and has answered with the mechanism instead, and people have found the mechanism more annoying than a number would have been, which she has never told anybody she notices.

The Field Registry is the office that keeps the burnt list, and its whole discipline is that a settlement funeral reads the dead as the frame said rather than as the funeral said. The frame reads structure. Every body in the setting leaves a fossil of its own history in its frame, and the fossil is what a reader works from: a split vessel where a sac ran, a taproot where a heartwood used to be, a second set of shoulders along a spine. A deadlight has none of that. The lattice is inert. It repaired nothing and it recorded nothing, and a reader working from the frame finds in a deadlight body an absence with no fossil in it at all, which is indistinguishable from a body that was never interesting.

So she reads the frame, and the frame says her subject had no structural history, and she writes that down, and the family hears it as a verdict on the person rather than a limit of the instrument. She has changed her method twice because of it. She used to soften it. She stopped softening it after the second softening was quoted back at her as a reading, which taught her that a soft reading is a reading somebody will build on. Now she states the limit first and the absence second, and the order has cost her four households' goodwill and bought her a record nobody has ever had to retract.

Her discipline is called Void Refinement, and it is the setting's first genuinely steep step on the mind path: everything in the sea that was not understood is emptied out, because mind purification is subtraction before it is anything else. She has been doing it since she was seated, which is a phrase that means something else in her subspecies than it does in a culture that expects its people to be still, because a three-point stance over splayed toes never loads a heel and a marshfolk cannot be still, and a deadlight's discipline is not sitting at all. She empties the sea while walking a corridor, which the people who trained her found either impressive or alarming and never asked which.

The pairing in her is anatomical and she can name both halves. The bloom that gives her subspecies an unmediated interior is the same bloom that renews nothing in it, so the discipline she practises is the only thing in her body that is not being worn out by use. Every other advantage the subspecies has is bought with the same ninety years: she sees in the dark because the colony is gone, and she dies at ninety because the colony is gone, and the thing that lets her do her work at all is the thing that is killing her on schedule. She has made her peace with being an argument rather than a person, and the two are not the same, and she is tired of having to say so.

What she wants is for one more deadlight to be seated, anywhere, in any office, so that the next funeral has a control. She has asked the Registry four times and been told each time that the intake is one body and the body is hers, and that this is not a complaint about her but about the arithmetic of the subspecies. She believes them. She has started keeping her own ledger anyway, in a hand nobody else can read, because a species with ninety years and a quarter of the parent's stock cannot afford to have exactly one witness.
history: Seated at the quarry intake at nineteen, which for her subspecies is young and for everyone else on that floor was a child holding a slab, and the pairing tutor who set her there explained once that a hollow body needs a hand on the stone and then never mentioned it again.

First asked for an ordinal at twenty-one, at a reading, by a widower who wanted a number to put on the slate. She gave him the mechanism. He wrote down the number he had expected and struck it out afterwards, in front of her, and did not apologise for it, and she has thought about the fact that he struck it rather than the fact that he wrote it for about eleven years.

Stopped softening a limit from a reading in her third decade after a softened one was quoted back to her as the Registry's finding. She put the limit first from that reading onward and the record has held for nineteen years without a single retraction, which is a longer clean run than she expected and which she attributes entirely to the order of the sentences.

Began keeping a private ledger in a cipher of her own devising after a season in which four readings came back with the same figure attached to four unrelated bodies, which is either a coincidence or a fault in the intake and which she could not rule out from inside the instrument.

Asked the Registry for a second deadlight on the intake for the fourth time this year and was told the arithmetic of the subspecies, which is true, and has begun treating the refusal as a date rather than a decision, because every subspecies she knows of has run out of something long before anybody decided to stop.

personality.summary: Exact, flat, and entirely without self-regard, which reads as cold until you notice that the absence is not coldness but bookkeeping: she has been the only witness of her own species for nineteen years and has decided that the accounting is the job and the grief is a separate line item.

can hold a body part still against a moving slab and has never once been asked to explain how

mannerisms: walks a reading rather than standing at it, the discipline and the method having merged into a single habit years ago
keeps one bare hand flat on a surface whenever she is reading a live body, and lifts it only when somebody speaks to her
says the limit first, always, and counts to three internally before saying the finding, which is a thing nobody taught her
goes very still and very quiet when a family begins to understand what she has said, and holds that stillness until they have finished
refuses a second helping at the intake table and eats it cold two hours later, standing up
motivations: wants a second deadlight seated anywhere in any office, so that the next reading has a control and her figures can be checked by somebody who is not herself
wants her private ledger reconciled against the Registry's by somebody competent, and has not told the Registry it exists
wants the ritual wording changed so that an absent fossil is named as a limit of the instrument rather than as a property of the dead, which is the whole of her nineteen years of method
wants to reach the end of her own ninety years having produced at least one body that does not require her to explain it
flaws: is the sole instrument of a measure that disposes of the dead of four households a season, and has not built a second instrument because nobody has been seated and she cannot seat herself

personality.voice: Flat, concrete, given to exact nouns: fossil, frame, limit, lattice, figure. States things as a pair with the limit first, because a pair that arrives in the other order is a sentence with a fact in front of it. Speaks in the third person about her own body when the body is the subject, which happens more than she notices. Says things like the frame has nothing to give you about your wife and that is a limit of what I am holding, not a finding about her, and it has never once required her to raise her voice.
taboos: will not give a finding before the limit of the instrument that produced it
will not soften a reading because of who is in the room
will not let another body take a reading for her under any circumstances
will not describe her species as a form of the lanternfolk, in either direction
will not be thanked for the limit, and has twice asked that it stop being treated as a courtesy

relationships.note: A lanternfolk body with a silicate lattice in place of the hyphal colony: lighter, colder, and entirely inert, grown around what replaced the fungus rather than recovering. It is the control case of the setting and she is the control of the controls: the only live one, seated once, reading the frames of everybody else.

The parent body, still alive at two hundred and fifty years because a colony renews what it goes through, and still unable to take the mind path because the colony answers before the question is finished. Every fossil she reads at a funeral is a lanternfolk fossil, and her own frame is the one in the record that carries none, which is the whole difference between her parents and herself stated in one object.

The office that keeps the burnt list, reading the dead as the frame said rather than as the funeral said. Her instrument is its instrument and it is the only one it has: a deadlight frame returns an absence with no fossil in it, and the Registry is the only body in the setting with a method for reading frames, so it is the only body that could ever read her.

Everything in the sea that was not understood is emptied out, and the purity floor rises to price it: the first step on the mind path that is genuinely steep, and the one practice that requires a body nothing is renewing. She has run it since she was seated. It is the only thing in her frame that is not being worn out by the using, which is either an argument for it or an argument about her.

A cultivator people who count how many of the realm's gates were already closed when somebody was born and treat the whole ladder as arriving late by definition. It is the only culture she has ever been at home in, because a deadlight is born with the whole ladder absent rather than closed, and the arithmetic comes out the same and the sentiment does not fit her at all.

A grey lichen that colonises worked stone wherever a large quantity of qi has been drawn through it, and it never washes off, so all four rings are legible from above as pale patches and the mark outlives the argument about what happened. She works stone for a living and has never seen it grow on a floor, and she has stopped finding that strange and would find it more strange if she had.

reference_stats.summary: A mind-path practitioner of a subspecies with no ladder to climb, who reads the frame of the dead for the only office that can read frames and who empties a sea of everything in it that she cannot name, in a body that renews nothing and has about thirty years left on the subspecies' ninety.
strengths: is the only living control for the Registry's entire method, so her figures cannot be checked against anything and cannot be quietly corrected either, which cuts both ways and she knows which way it cuts more often than she admits
sees in a quarry in total darkness, where a lanternfolk parent would be reading its own light off a wall and a lit body would be blind
works a live body by touch at a slab and does not fatigue, because nothing in the frame is being repaired and there is therefore nothing for the fatigue to spend
has never had a reading retracted, which is the longest clean run in that office and is a direct consequence of stating the limit first for nineteen years
weaknesses: carries no fossil, so the instrument that disposes of four households a season returns nothing about any of them, and she is the one who has to say so out loud
has been the sole instance of her subspecies' frame for nineteen years and cannot tell her own figures from the fault in the instrument, because she is both
is stopped at no ordinal and so has no rung on which her progress could be measured by anybody including herself
carries a permanent scar on the left wrist and a permanently slow-growing crop and neither of them will improve, which is the subspecies' arithmetic stated on her body
reference_stats.combat_read: She does not close and she will not. Nothing that arrives at her has to be answered quickly, because an unanswered question costs her nothing and a wrong reading costs four households. Let her put a hand on you and the reading begins, and the reading is the fight: she will find the split vessel, the taproot, or the fossil, and whatever she finds is what the record becomes. Do not give her time on a live body, and do not give her the chance to say the limit first, because she always says it first and it is always true.
notes: The advantage and its cost are the same organ. The mineral bloom that gives her subspecies an unmediated interior and therefore the mind path is the bloom that renews nothing, so the ninety-year lifespan and the untroubled reading are one fact. This is the subspecies' authored anatomy and no rule has been added here to make it work.
Her species has no ordinal to quote. That is an absence in the race record, not a ceiling of zero, and it is why the realm field is written as a mechanism rather than as a number.

There is no second deadlight in the Registry's service and the refusal to seat one is stated as arithmetic rather than as a decision, which she has believed for nineteen years and has recently begun treating as a date.

identity.realm: Comprehension and will carry this body through bands a hotter lineage could not reach, and her species has no authored ordinal to quote at any of them, because the ceiling field on the tidecaller record is an absence rather than a number: a body assembled for looking is unconstrained by anything in its own frame, so there is no wall of hers to arrive at. She is at Spirit Unity on the mind ladder and the ladder's own ladder is the only ordinal in her life.

appearance.presentation: A tidecaller is a long-lived body built for perception rather than for force, and this is one of the few in the setting whose whole station is the length of an attention rather than the weight of a blow. She is the confederacy's long read: one body that will hold an unbroken observation across a tide change and a night both, and who cannot be struck out of the reckoning because the reckoning is her.
appearance.age: One hundred and ninety-four on a species lifespan of a little over a century and a half of practised years, which is past the point where anybody expected a tidecaller to still be working and which she has never brought up and has never once been asked about, because nobody who asks her a question about the water has ever thought to ask her one about herself.
appearance.build: Long and narrow through the chest, built along the line of a spine that carries an eye rather than a load, with narrow hands and an unusually steady neck. She is not frail in the ordinary way and has been in two wrecks and walked out of both, and nobody has ever seen that as contradictory.
appearance.complexion: Pale and weathered flat rather than lined, the way a body that spends its life in reflected light ages. Water affinity is the only affinity she holds, which shows as a skin that tightens in dry air rather than tanning in it.
appearance.hair: Long, and the one vanity she admits to, kept braided flat because anything loose is a thing the wind on that coast takes an interest in. It is the colour of wet slate.
appearance.eyes: Wide-set and still, with lids that do not blink on a fixed count she has never been aware of. The species' gift is comprehension carried by will and this is what it looks like from the outside: somebody whose eyes stop moving and whose attention does not.
appearance.palette: Sea-grey and wet slate with one warm value, lamp-amber, kept low and behind her. The whole coast is grey and she is darker than it, and the art should never light her from the front: every shot of her is lit by something she is looking at.
appearance.attire: A long coat of oiled wool to the knee, sea boots worn through at the left sole, and a chart case that has been mended with a cord rather than a stitch. Sleeves are full and buttoned at the wrist and she undoes them to work, which is the only concession to warmth she appears to make at all.
appearance.marks: Two inches of old rope burn across the inside of the left forearm from a wreck line, and the palms of both hands are darker than the backs, permanently, from eleven years of wet chart paper.
appearance.bearing: Absolutely level, and unusually still for somebody standing on a working shoreline. She plants her feet apart at the waterline and does not shift her weight, which on that coast is read as competence and is actually just a habit that lets her hold a line of sight for nine hundred seconds without her neck betraying her.

canon.role_in_story: The Two Shores is a league of both coasts of the Cloudshelf Sea, formed the moment the sea became worth owning, and the one thing the two coasts agree on is that they need each other without either conceding the water. Every allocation of a kelp bed, every dispute over where the tideline now sits, and every date a boat may cross comes down to one question that only one body on either shore can answer: what is the water actually doing right now. Selka Marrow is that body. She holds an unbroken read across a tide change and a night both, which makes her the only instrument in the setting capable of distinguishing a rising shelf from a falling one while it is happening, and which makes her the single point of failure in a league that has spent four generations arranging itself so that no single body is one.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing at the waterline of a bed neither shore claims with her feet planted and her hands at her sides, saying that the drift was moving before the level was, and being asked by two delegates at once which of the two she meant.
canon.lore:
A tidecaller was assembled for looking rather than for being hit. Comprehension and will carry the body through bands that would end a hotter frame, water affinity is the only affinity it holds, and it cannot take the body path at all, because the whole of the construction went into the apparatus of attention and nothing was left for the apparatus of impact. That is not a limitation discovered later. It is the design.

The setting has no ordinal to quote for what she is. A tidecaller's ceiling is written as an absence rather than as a number, because a body built for looking is not constrained by anything in its own frame; there is no wall of hers to arrive at, and no gate of hers to fail. So the only ladder in her life is the one she has personally climbed, and every figure she has given for it is her own. She has told two people this in nineteen years. Both wrote it down.

The sea is the setting's first genuinely arguable boundary, and the argument is about kelp. The Cloudshelf Kelp grows in the tideline and stops the moment the Tidemark turns against it, which makes it the only food source that can be farmed and defended at once: the shore is worth more than the fish in it, and whoever draws the tideline draws the harvest, the season and the price. The Cloudshelf Hunter is licensed rather than tolerated, which makes the hunt a calendar problem and makes the water controllable for a window rather than outright.

The Two Shores exists because of that kelp. Two coasts, one sea, a league rather than a war, formed the moment the water became worth owning and admitting a need without conceding anything. And a league has a particular weakness, which is that its authority is the sum of its members' agreeing and a single dissenter is not a minority. So the confederacy spent four generations building a structure where no one body's word is the word: panels, second reads, a published drift, a chartered town at the mouth of the only verifiable hole in the setting.

And then there is her.

Because a kelp bed has a written season and a moving waterline, the question of what a shore is worth is not answerable from a table. It is answerable only by watching, for long enough, to tell a drift from a level. Nine surveys of one bed over one season will disagree, and the disagreement is not noise: it is the measurement, because the thing being measured changes while it is being measured. The only instrument in the setting that can hold one line of sight across a tide change and a night both is a tidecaller, because the body was built to hold one.

So the league that arranged itself so that no single body could be load-bearing has made one exactly load-bearing, and did so by being reasonable. She is asked to hold the read. She holds the read. It is nine hundred seconds on a good night and eleven hundred when the water is arguing with itself, and when she comes off it she gives them a drift before she gives them a level, because the drift is the finding and the level is only where the drift happens to be at the end.

The pairing is anatomical and she has never had to argue for it. Her comprehension and her will carry her through gates that would end a body built for anything else, and the same long attention that carries her there is the one that leaves her unable to be wrong about water in the particular way that matters here. A body that reads perfectly is a body nobody can check, because there is no second tidecaller on either shore to read it against. She is the instrument and the calibration and there is no third thing.

What she wants is somebody to read her. Not to replace her and not to second her: to hold a line of sight on her while she holds one on the water, so that the one claim in the league that has never been falsified has a falsifier. She has asked the confederacy twice, in writing, and been told both times that a tidecaller who cannot be checked is a tidecaller who cannot be replaced, and that the league had spent a century not building that.
history: First held a full tide change at nineteen, on a bed that was disputed then and is disputed still, and gave the drift before she gave the level without being asked for either, which is the only part of that night anybody repeats when they repeat the night.

Lost eleven hundred and forty pounds of kelp to a season in which she was the only reader and the only reader was ill, and the league's answer was to ask her a second question about the same night rather than to ask whether she should have been asked the first.

Began stating the drift before the level in her third decade, after a bed was allocated on a level she had given and it was found she had been watching the wrong quantity all day: a level is where the water happens to be and a drift is which way it is going, and only one of those is an allocation.

Asked the confederacy for a second reader in writing for the first time and was refused on the grounds that an uncheckable reader cannot be replaced, which she wrote down and kept, because it is the most accurate thing anybody has ever said about her and she would rather it were on the record than in her own head.

Has held every contested read on this coast for eleven years, and in the last one gave a figure eleven seconds short of her own best and has not been able to account for the eleven seconds, which is the first thing she has ever published from that body that she could not afterwards reconstruct.

personality.summary: Still, level and faintly amused, with a patience that reads as expensive because it genuinely is: she can afford to wait longer than the argument can afford to disagree. She has the manner of somebody who has never once had to raise her voice about water and has organised an entire professional life around not needing to.

personality.voice: Level, unhurried, and given to exact nouns: drift, level, bed, window, second. States things as a pair with the movement first, because a pair that arrives the other way round answers a question nobody asked. Speaks about water in the present tense and about people in the past, and has been doing it since she was a girl. Says things like the drift is moving and the level is only where it happens to be, which is the whole of her argument and has never once needed repeating.
taboos: will not give a level without the drift that produced it
will not shorten a read because a boat is waiting, whatever the boat
will not let a second body read for her under any circumstances
will not be told what she saw on a night she has already published, and will decline to restate a figure rather than defend it
will not be asked about her age, and treats the asking as a breach of the water rather than of her privacy

relationships.note: A long-lived body assembled for perception rather than for force, holding water affinity as its only affinity and comprehension and will as the two things that carry it. It cannot take the body path at all, because the whole construction went into attention. Her advantage and her isolation are the same organ: the reading is perfect and there is no second body on either shore capable of confirming it.

A league of the two coasts of the Cloudshelf Sea, formed the moment the sea became worth owning, on the principle that both shores may admit a need without either conceding the water. Four generations of panels and second reads and no single dissenter, and then one tidecaller that every contested allocation comes down to, which is what happens when an institution asks for the most reasonable thing available.

It grows in the tideline and stops the moment the Tidemark turns against it, which makes it the one food source that can be farmed and defended at once. Everything she is asked for is asked about where this stops, and the answer is a line in moving water, which is the one quantity in the setting no table has ever held.

The sea's apex predator, licensed rather than tolerated because a shelf that can be farmed has to have something that eats what it farms. Its entire population is a function of the kelp and therefore of the season, so the hunt is a calendar problem and the water is controllable for a window rather than outright. She determines the window and has never been asked to defend it in public.

The compartments hold together as one awareness instead of several, which is the state Mind Dao calls unity and Body Dao calls a cage. She is above it and there is no ordinal for where she is, so the ladder's numbering is the only record of her achievement and she is the only person who could write it and the only person who would be believed writing it.

A stone-shored coastal people who read water, sand and wind for a living because after the Iron Grief that reading was the only work on the plains that still bought passage. They read by eye and taught it by standing in it, and they are the reason a shore reading is a profession at all, which is the profession she is the last professional member of.

reference_stats.summary: A mind-path reader of a body assembled for looking, holding a line of sight across a tide change and a night both in a league that cannot do without her and cannot check her, on a species with no authored ordinal for anything she has done.
strengths: holds one unbroken line of sight for over eleven hundred seconds, which is longer than any read this coast has ever recorded and long enough to distinguish a drift from a level while the difference is still happening
cannot be hurried by weather, by a waiting boat, or by a delegate, and has never once shortened a read for any of them
reports the movement before the measurement, so an allocation built on her figure cannot be built on a snapshot that was already out of date when it was taken
reads a shoreline for what it is doing rather than for what it is worth, which is the only reason any allocation on this coast has ever survived a season
weaknesses: is the sole instrument of the only contested measurement the confederacy has, so every allocation on both shores depends on a figure that no second body is capable of checking
has a published read eleven seconds short of her own best and cannot reconstruct where the eleven seconds went
closes the body path outright, so there is no answer available to her that does not consist of continuing to look
has outlived every reader who might have learned the method from her, because her species produces them at a rate of about one in a generation and she has kept the method
reference_stats.combat_read: She cannot close and does not need to. Everything that comes at her crosses water first, and she has spent a century learning that water lies about distance and is honest about direction, so she knows what is approaching long before it arrives and has never once had to guess. The only pressure that works on her is time: make her choose between a short read and a true one and she will take the true one every time, which means you must be willing to be waited out. A patient reader on a shoreline beats anything that has to breathe for four hundred seconds against her and still be moving.
notes: The advantage and its cost are the same anatomy. Comprehension and will carry her through bands a hotter frame could not reach, and the same long attention is what makes her the only reader either shore has and therefore the only reader neither shore can check. Both halves are the tidecaller's authored construction; no rule has been invented here to make the pairing work.

The tidecaller record writes its ceiling as an absence, not as a figure, so there is no ordinal to quote for anything she has reached and the realm field is written that way on purpose. It would be wrong to invent a rung for her species.

Her discipline on the water is the same one she practises off it: hold a line without looking away. Nothing in the bible states that as a technique, so it is written here as a habit with a cost and not as a rule with a number.

name: Vashti Mora
aliases: the one who takes it out first

identity.realm: Eleventh gate, and the wall at the eleventh is the wall of her whole species rather than of her: the brine sac runs dorsal to the sternum the length of the spine and splits the penetrating vessel into two halves that cannot be rejoined. She clears the du and the ren one at a time and stalls on the chong, and no discipline has ever been found that gets a saltfolk past it. Everything above that rung on her ladder is a thing she has heard about.

appearance.presentation: A saltfolk of the basin's courts, which is a people built for brine no softer body could drink, standing in a working dress with a waxed tongue-guard at her throat. She is the dominion's subtraction clerk: the officer who decides which parts of a household's claim are removed before a grant is issued, which is a mind-path discipline before it is an administrative one and the only office on that ground that has ever described itself as emptying.
appearance.age: Fifty-seven pan seasons, which is not a year: the water decides how long a season is, and she is younger than that figure and older than the pit she works, and the discrepancy between the two is the only number about her she quotes without being asked.
appearance.build: Broad through the ribs and low and wide at the pelvis, with the brine sac standing as a second set of shoulders along the upper spine, so that she is visibly more person above the waist than below. Her feet are splayed and broader than any boot the pan makes, and she stands with her weight even, which she learned on purpose as a girl and has never stopped needing.
appearance.complexion: Grey-white under a hard dermal salt crust, translucent at the temples and cracked through in the dry months, so that she reads as a cracked vessel rather than as a face. Rain is a hazard to her species rather than a blessing and she has been caught in one twice.
appearance.hair: Coarse and salt-stiffened, cut blunt at the jaw because it grows in a hard ring and anything longer breaks at the ends. It is the only soft thing about her and it is not soft at all.
appearance.eyes: Small, deep-set and quick, and plainly not her working instrument: the species' vision is no better than a Commonborn's and poor in glare, so she does her work with her mouth and her eyes only find a face afterwards.
appearance.palette: Crust white and brine grey across the figure with the single warm value being mineral ochre from a cut face, which is the only colour on the pan and therefore the only colour on her. Nothing else in any shot of her is saturated, which is the visual statement of a body with nothing to spend.
appearance.attire: A clerk's waxed coat over salt-cured hide, laced above the elbow so the crust can be scraped, and a broad tongue-guard of waxed cloth she has refused to work without five times. She does not taste brine through cloth and will not pretend to, which is why the court's work is slower than a house that would let somebody else take the figure.
appearance.marks: The dermal crust itself, re-cracked every dry season and never smoothed, and three healed splits at the corners of her mouth from tasting what she had been told not to, which is the mark of a woman who has twice been wrong in public on the one subject she is the only person on the ground qualified to be wrong about.
appearance.bearing: Still, for a saltfolk, which is a thing she trained rather than inherited. She crouches to read water rather than kneeling in it, stands with her weight even because a figure read off a moving body is a figure she cannot stand behind, and turns her face up into rain when it comes because the alternative is hiding from it in a body that cannot leave.

canon.role_in_story: A household's standing in the salt dominion is the depth of water it may moor at, and the basin's level rises and falls, so an allotment shrinks without anybody having done anything at all. The dominion's depth-books are therefore never wrong and never settle, and the office that keeps them has to do the one thing nobody on that ground wants done: take pieces out. Vashti Mora is the subtraction clerk. She decides which parts of a claim come out before a grant is issued, and she has built the whole of the court's method out of a mind-path discipline the Quench Order never touches, because Void Refinement is subtraction before it is anything else and a dominion whose wealth is a number has needed subtraction since before anybody thought to name it. Her discipline and her office are the same operation, which is why she is so good at one and so bad at the other.
canon.first_appearance: First seen crouched at a figure board at the lip of a settling pan with two fingers in the brine and her tongue-guard hanging loose, reciting a claim back to a house head with two thirds of it struck out, and refusing to hand the slate over until he had read the struck-out lines as well as the ones that survived.
canon.lore:
A saltfolk is built for brine no softer body could drink. The kidneys concentrate salt past the point ordinary water poisons, and that is the entire bargain: total dependence on a supply that never fails, and a body that is already failing the moment the supply changes. They read brine concentration across four orders of dilution, to a human nose a saltfolk smells sour, and they cannot leave: a saltfolk carried above the brine line begins to fail within about nine days, and rain is a hazard rather than a blessing, because a saltfolk caught in a downpour is functionally drowning. They are the least mobile people in the setting and they are a species of a resource rather than a nation of it, because they exist because the brine does.

The dominion's territory is exactly its waterline and its standing is a depth. A household may moor at a depth, that depth is held as an inheritance, and it is passed down with the body that has to live in it. So the grant and the dependence arrive together and cannot be separated: the basin's level rises and falls, an allotment shrinks without anybody having done anything, and two bodies reading the same basin disagree about which depth-book is the right one at a pier. The prize in that dispute is which book is read, and it cannot be split because a depth is one measurement of one body of water.

The office that keeps those books has a job nobody wants. A claim arrives too large, because the level moved, and something has to come out of it, and somebody has to be the person who chose. That is Vashti Mora, and she has been doing it for nineteen seasons, and she is very good at it.

She is good at it because of a discipline that has nothing to do with brine. Void Refinement is the mind path's first genuinely steep step, and its whole method is that everything in the sea which was not understood is emptied out, because mind purification is subtraction before it is anything else and the purity floor rises to price it. She came to the office at nineteen already doing it to herself and found, about four years later, that she had been doing it to other people's claims for two seasons before anyone corrected her. The discipline and the job are the same operation. That is why she is so much better at the one than at the other.

The discipline is open to her species and complete. The path's whole apparatus sits high in the chest to keep clear of the brine sac, and the soul is seated there for exactly that reason. The wall is not the mind's: it is anatomical, and it is at the eleventh gate on every ladder in her life, because the sac runs dorsal to the sternum the length of the spine and splits the penetrating vessel into two halves. She clears the du and the ren one at a time and stalls on the chong. There is no discipline that gets a saltfolk past it and she has stopped looking.

And the discipline she runs her office on has a property the Quench Order would recognise instantly and cannot use, which is that the body it empties cannot be refilled by the person doing the emptying. A Quench banker spends a furnace deliberately before it overflows. A saltfolk clerk's problem is never overflow. It is drying out, and it is nine days long, and it is not a discipline at all, it is a shoreline.

The pairing in her is anatomical and she has never made a secret of it. Her species' kidneys concentrate salt past the point ordinary water poisons, which is what makes her figure exact and her people the only ones on that ground who can state where the boundary between drinkable and poison sits. The same concentration is what makes her unable to be anywhere but there, and it is why the instrument she reads the water with goes blunt in exactly the freshening air a claim is argued in. She is sharp on the side of the line she can live on and blunt on the side where the argument is.

What she wants is for the struck-out lines to be kept. The depth-books record what remains and destroy what came out, on the doctrine that a claim which can be reduced is not a claim. She has kept every removal she has made for nineteen seasons in a hand nobody reads, with the air state written beside each one, and she has asked twice for the court to hold them and been refused twice on the ground that a house which can see what was taken from it will litigate instead of moor.

On that she is probably right. She has checked the arithmetic more than once and she still keeps the ledger, and she has never told the court it exists, and she has begun to think that a clerk who is right about this and alone about it is not in a better position than one who is wrong and shared.
history: Taught the subtraction to herself at fifteen as a way of getting through an ordinary evening, on the reasoning that a thing she could empty was a thing she did not have to keep thinking about. She has never met anybody who teaches it that way and does not know it is unusual.

Took the court's clerkship at nineteen because it was the only post on the basin paying by the grant, and discovered in her second season that emptying a claim was the same operation as emptying a sea, and that nobody around her considered this a coincidence worth mentioning.

Struck out two thirds of a house's claim in her fourth season and read the struck lines out to the house head herself rather than handing over a slate, on the reasoning that a man who does not hear what was removed cannot argue that it was removed wrongly, and has done it that way in every season since.

Started keeping the removals in her own hand in her ninth season, after a year in which the basin's level rose enough that eleven separate claims had been reduced and nobody could later say whether the reductions had been the basin's doing or hers.

Asked the court twice to hold the struck-out lines and been refused twice on the ground that a house which can see what was taken from it will litigate instead of moor. She checked the arithmetic again after the second refusal and found the court right, and has kept the ledger anyway, and has not told them it exists.

She presents as a slow, courteous, faintly boring woman who does a difficult job on purpose and would like to stop being asked about it, and the courtesy is the armour and not the manner.

personality.voice: Flat, concrete, given to exact nouns: concentration, order, figure, air, depth. States things as pairs, because a pair is what a reading is here, and speaks about herself in the third person when the figure is in the room. Says things like I will tell you what I struck and then you may argue with it, which is the whole of her method and which she has never once had to raise her voice to make.
taboos: will not give a figure without the air-state that produced it
will not hand over a slate before the struck lines have been read aloud

will not be thanked for reading the struck lines, and has asked three times that it stop being treated as a kindness

relationships.note: A people built for brine no softer body could drink, whose kidneys concentrate salt past the point ordinary water poisons so the supply never fails and nothing else lives. Total dependence on that supply is the whole bargain: carried onto fresh ground a saltfolk is already failing and no cultivation repairs it. Her instrument is the species' sense and its own blindness, and she is the only person on the ground who has to state both every morning.

Everything in the sea that was not understood is emptied out, and the purity floor rises to price it: purification is subtraction before it is anything else, and the first step on the path that is genuinely steep. She learned it as an evening exercise at fifteen and found four years later that she had been emptying other people's claims with it for two seasons without telling anybody, which is either the clearest case in the record of a discipline and a job being one operation or the clearest case of a clerk who found a technique that flattered her.

A dominion whose territory is its waterline, where a household's standing is the depth it may moor at and that depth is held as an inheritance and passed down with the body that has to live in it. The grant and the dependence arrive together, the level rises and falls, and the book that has to be read at a pier is the prize in every dispute between them. She writes in it every season and has removed more from it than anybody alive.

An allotment can shrink without anybody having done anything at all, and the two sides are the dominion and the tideline culture that speaks in high, low and turning instead of dates. It cannot be split because a depth is one measurement of one body of water. She is not a party to it and has never been asked which side she thinks is right, because asking would make her one, and she has twice declined a private opinion from the tideline side in language that took an afternoon to write.

A discipline of Bankers rather than a school of thought, teaching the deliberate spending of a furnace before it overflows and closing permanently the moment the body is lit. It is the setting's one practice built around not overfilling, and a saltfolk's condition is the opposite: going empty, on a nine-day clock, with no practice attached to it. She has the training and none of the subject, which is why she is the one body on the pan that can convert the difference into a discipline.

The only body in the record that metabolises brine and fresh water alike, produced by crossing the salt-adapted people with the fully watered ones because both parents are trapped by their own element. Its reading of a line would be independent of the air, which is exactly what this basin lacks and exactly what would make a reduction attributable to the water rather than to the reader. Nobody has ever asked one, because a house that can attribute its loss to the water stops disputing the clerk.

reference_stats.summary: A mind-path subtraction clerk stopped at the structural eleventh gate of her species, who empties claims for a living by the same operation she empties her own sea by, and who is exact in saturated air and blunt in exactly the freshening air a claim gets argued in.
strengths: reads four orders of dilution across a span no instrument on that ground can cover, so her figure is the only one that cannot be corroborated, contradicted or even approximated by another body
states the air-state with every figure, which makes it possible after the fact to tell a dull reading from a wrong one, a distinction nobody on the basin had before her
does not tire and does not spike and works the same in the glare the species reads worst in
can name which of any two readings belongs to a day when the water was changing, which is the only distinction the basin actually needs and the one every other figure there is missing
weaknesses: the blind side of her instrument is the side the water is leaving, so the moment a reduction matters most is the moment she is least able to see it
is stopped at the eleventh gate by a sac behind her own sternum that splits the penetrating vessel into halves, on every ladder and not only this one
has no second body able to read her ground independently, so a single dull reading is indistinguishable from a single correct one once the season has turned
cannot drink fresh water, cannot leave the pan, and is functionally drowning in a downpour, which removes every option she does not currently have anyway
reference_stats.combat_read: She will not close and she does not need to. Everything that comes at her is announced by the air it arrives in, and a salted frame carries four orders of dilution in its crust, so anything that came off the pan she can place before it lands. The only pressure that works is freshening: get fresh water between her and the brine, let the air thin out, and the woman who reads four orders suddenly reads one and a half and knows she is doing it. Do not outlast her. The pan is hers, she is patient, and a patient reader of standing brine beats anything that has to breathe against her and still be moving.
notes: The advantage and its cost are one organ. The kidneys that concentrate salt past the point ordinary water poisons are the reason her figure is exact and the reason she cannot be anywhere but here, and the salt head that dulls fine discrimination in freshening air fails on precisely the boundary she is being paid to declare. Both halves are the saltfolk's authored anatomy; no mechanical rule has been invented here to close the pairing.

Her wall at the eleventh is anatomical and species-wide: the brine sac splits the penetrating vessel into halves, so she clears du and ren one at a time and stalls on the chong. The ordinal is real and is stated rather than approximated.

Her office and her discipline are both subtraction, and that is an observation about a court and a mind-path step rather than a rule either text states. It is written here as her practice, with a cost attached, and not as a mechanic.

identity.realm: Thirteenth gate, and stopped there for a reason that belongs to her body rather than to her species. Ordinal seventeen is the first gate needing both flank vessels pressurised at once, and a longwinter manages one warm gradient for a few weeks in summer and then not again for a year; that is her species' wall and she has never reached it. Hers is closer and it is her own doing: the discipline she sits needs her awake and warm, and she has not hibernated in eleven years, which is the entire difference between her and every other longwinter on this ridge and the reason the two warm gradients are further out of her reach than they would otherwise be.

appearance.presentation: A cold-climate body that stores a winter as body fat rather than as qi, standing awake in a shed doorway on a ridge where the species it belongs to would be eleven weeks from torpor and she is not. She is one of the Pass Sheds' winter bodies: an institution that holds a border by paying its holders in labour rotation, never in coin, staffed by whoever can be relied on in the worst hours of the year, and the only longwinter on this ridge who can.
appearance.age: Seventy-one, which for a longwinter is middle age and which she has begun mentioning as a fact rather than a figure, because she is the oldest awake body on the ridge and the arithmetic of that is a thing she would rather state than be asked.
appearance.build: Broad and low-framed with heavy subcutaneous fat and reduced limb length, warm-blooded and cheap to run. She is thinner than her sisters by a season's worth and the difference is visible in the face first, and she has stopped being able to eat her way back into a year of it in about nine days.
appearance.complexion: Frost-flushed across the cheeks and nose and pale between them, and it does not go away indoors because the cold in her is a matter of circulation rather than of air. Her hands are always warm to touch, which is the single most confusing thing about her on a ridge in the dark.
appearance.hair: Pale, coarse and grown out long past the point of practicality, kept in a single braid that she does not plait properly and has never been asked to. It is the colour of the snow that accumulated on her this morning and stayed.
appearance.eyes: Half-lidded and pale, and the half-lidded part is a species trait and the awake part is something she has trained for eleven years. Her species reads by smell and its vision is mediocre; she tracks a route across open ground by scent and has stopped apologising for it being the other way round.
appearance.palette: Snow white and undyed wool with one warm value, lantern amber, and it belongs to the lantern and never to her. On a ridge in the dark the whole of her is a warm shape with a lantern in it, which is the practical reason she is the winter body and also the reason nobody looks at her face for eleven months.
appearance.attire: Layered undyed wool to the throat with a coat over it, fastened right up even in the shed, and a pair of felted overshoes worn through at the left sole. She keeps her coat on indoors in the worst hours because undressing is the first step of going under and she has trained herself out of that step over a period of years, deliberately and against advice.
appearance.marks: A ridge of pale burn across both forearms from a shed stove she fell asleep against in her first winter, and the burns have not faded in eleven years because nothing in her body is renewed quickly. She shows them to nobody and has described them exactly twice, both times unprompted and both times to explain a rule rather than the scar.
appearance.bearing: Slow, unhurried, and consistently present, which is the whole of her usefulness and reads as dullness on anyone who has not spent a winter with her. She sits down without warning and gets up without hurry and has caught herself twice standing in a doorway unable to say which of those was going to happen.

canon.role_in_story: The Pass Sheds are the material basis of a faith with no doctrine: sheds on the Sixfold Ridge paid for in labour rotation and never in coin, which is how a body that has no garrison can hold a border, and the whole arrangement rests on one question with one answer. Who is awake in the worst hours of the year. Yanne Coldwick is that answer on this ridge, and she is awake in the worst hours for a reason nobody on the ridge finds reasonable: a longwinter survives the winter by going under, storing the season as fat and lowering her core temperature for eleven months, and a hibernating longwinter is a large, warm, immobile target that cannot be woken quickly. So the species that built itself for the cold is the one species that cannot be relied on in it, and she is the longwinter who decided the discipline was worth more than the sleep.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in a shed doorway at the turn of the gale with a lantern in one hand and her coat still fastened, answering a question about the north window in about four seconds and then apologising for the four seconds in a way that suggests she has apologised before.
canon.lore:
A longwinter is a body that survives on a hibernate-and-store cycle. It packs a winter as body fat rather than as qi, lowers its core temperature and goes into torpor for eleven months, and comes up in the thaw to eleven weeks of enormous appetite and then goes back under. That single decision is what puts the flank vessels out of reach: they need two warm gradients held at once, and a longwinter has one, briefly, in summer, and then not again for a year. They reach far and never stay there.

It also makes them the best long-haul traders in the setting and makes them, in the specific way that has organised her life, useless in the winter. A hibernating longwinter is slow and nearly helpless during torpor. It cannot be woken quickly. It is a large, warm, immobile target in a country whose weather is the only thing anybody is paid to watch.

The Pass Sheds exist because of that arithmetic. A faith with no doctrine holds a ridge because sheds are paid for in labour rotation and never in coin, and because a holder of a toll needs somewhere to stand in the worst hours of the year. The arrangement has one staffing question in it and the answer has to be a person, and on this ridge the person is a longwinter who stopped going under.

Her discipline is a sitting. Clear Mind is the cheapest passive in the codex and the least dramatic thing in the setting: a daily sitting that empties the head before the day starts, raising mental clarity and sharpening a read on the room. There is no achievement in it, no gate, no gate-fee. You do it every day or you do not do it, and a species that spends eleven months a year unable to do anything at all is a species whose entire practice is interrupted for the majority of its life.

So she does it standing. That is the first thing and it is not the interesting thing. The interesting thing is that after about four years she noticed she could not do it standing either, not because standing is wrong but because she was doing it in a room at four in the afternoon in the eighth month of the year with her coat off, which is the exact posture a longwinter's body begins to go under in. She had been sitting up because the shed was cold and because she was busy, and she had been misreading the two as the same thing.

The thing she does instead is small and unglamorous and she has never once described it as a technique. She keeps the coat on. She keeps the lantern lit. She sits in a cold shed in the worst hours and empties her head on purpose, and the discipline works because the two things that would let her go under have both been made impossible. The coat and the light are not symbols. They are the two conditions her body needs met before it will drop, and she has spent eleven years learning what those conditions are from the inside, which is a thing her species does not generally know because its members do not generally get to choose.

The pairing is anatomical and it is not close to even. What she gains is eleven unbroken years of a discipline that compounds, on a species whose breakthroughs are late and rarely fail because qi accumulates rather than circulates and whose soul is held very deep and very quiet and is difficult to read and exceptionally hard to damage. What it costs is the eleven weeks of stored fat she no longer builds, so she goes into every winter thin for a longwinter, which is the exact condition the fat exists to prevent, and she is the only awake body on a ridge where a sleeping one would be safer.

Her wall is her species' wall and she is further from it than they are. Ordinal seventeen needs both flank vessels pressurised at once. Every other longwinter gets one warm gradient in summer and loses the rest of the year. She does not get that gradient properly at all, because the warm gradient is the fat and the fat is the thing she has stopped making, and so the top of her ladder is a gate she could almost reach and has now put further away by the only discipline she trusts.

She has never called that a failure and she is not going to. What she says, when she says anything about it, is that she is not going under and the ridge is held and somebody has to be awake, and that those two facts are the same fact, and that a person who can do both is worth more than one who can do either. She has been asked twice by the rotation whether she would take a summer post if the winter one were doubled and has said no both times in a single word each, and the word was the same both times.

What she has not told anybody is what she intends to do about the thinness. She has a plan for it. The plan involves the eleven weeks and it is not a good plan and she has not written it down, and the reason she has not written it down is that she has spent eleven years keeping herself awake by not undressing and she is not sure she can hold a decision she has put on paper.
history: Went into her first torpor at fourteen and came up in the thaw having forgotten the shape of a face she had looked at every day for a week beforehand, which is the ordinary longwinter experience and the first thing that made her think the eleven months were a kind of death rather than a rest.

Began the daily sitting in her twenties because the longwinter who held the north shed before her had done it and had died in the seat, and she has never worked out whether that is why she started or whether she has simply told herself that story for forty years because the true one is duller.

Fell asleep against a shed stove in her first winter as a holder and burned both forearms. The burns did not fade, because nothing in her body is renewed quickly, and she has used them since as the reason for a rule rather than as an injury.

Stopped hibernating in her sixtieth year, over eleven days, without telling the rotation and without a plan she could write down. The coat and the lantern came first and the decision came after them, which she has since realised is how she has made every important one.

Was offered a doubled summer post two years ago and refused it in one word, and has noticed since that she cannot remember whether the word was no or not yet, and has decided not to look for a witness who could tell her.

relationships.note: A cold-climate body that packs a winter as body fat rather than as qi, lowering its core temperature for eleven months and going helpless in torpor. That single decision puts the flank vessels out of reach and makes the species the setting's best long-haul traders and its worst winter staff. Her advantage and her whole liability are the same biology: qi accumulates rather than circulates, so her breakthroughs are late and rarely fail, and it is the accumulation she has spent eleven years not interrupting.

Sheds on the Sixfold Ridge paid for in labour rotation and never in coin, which is how a faith with no doctrine holds a border no garrison will staff. The arrangement has exactly one staffing question in it, and it is who is awake in the worst hours of the year. She answered it by stopping being a body that goes under, and the rotation has been treating that as a favour ever since.

A daily sitting that empties the head before the day starts: mental clarity and a sharper read on the room, and the cheapest passive in the codex. No gate, no gate-fee, no achievement. It requires doing every day or not at all, which for a species that spends eleven months unable to do anything is a discipline interrupted for the majority of a life. She has done it every day for eleven years, standing, in a cold shed, with her coat on.

The bird that has been using these sheds for longer than the rotation has, and which arrives at a sill in weather that stops everything else. Her species reads by smell and its vision is mediocre, so she tracks the ridge by scent and hears the swift before she sees it, and there is a version of the winter watch that depends entirely on noticing that early and not on looking harder.

The window is a season with an opening and a closing, and everything on that ridge turns on it. Her species cannot hold ordinal seventeen because the two warm gradients it needs exist for a few weeks in summer, and she has given up the fat those gradients are made of. She is paid to watch the one thing that is closing on her body.

The second house on the ridge, holding the pass ground while the calendar sits with the reeves, because a family holding both the ground and the schedule would be unassailable. They have agreed with the first house for three generations to argue only about price, which means the ground she stands on is deliberately not held by the same people who decide when she is needed, and she has never once been sure that is a safeguard or an oversight.

name: Erith Ambrose
aliases: the one who cannot hold still

identity.realm: Ninth gate on the mind ladder, and the figure is the least interesting thing about her. Her species pools qi low and wide in a broad pelvic basin rather than a compact chest seat, so it takes charge out of wet ground efficiently and out of dry ground poorly, which is the whole of her supply. Her species' structural wall is at the fourteenth gate, which needs both heel vessels pressurised at once, and a three-point stance over splayed toes and a tail-prop never loads a heel: they walk fine and they cannot stand still. She is nine gates below that and the mind ladder does not care, which is the only reason she has a path at all.

appearance.presentation: A wading amphibian lineage that breathes air and nests on floating mats, so it is neither a tidecaller nor a Commonborn but the body in between: long-legged, three-point, permanently damp, and the only mind-path practitioner on the Widow Run. She is the sect's unwritten member and the sect recognises nothing at all, which is why her advancement exists and why no document anywhere holds it.
appearance.age: Thirty-one, which for her species is late rather than young, because marshfolk eggs are carried under the brood pouch through the dry season and hatched when the water returns, and a mis-timed clutch is the ordinary arithmetic of her people. She was hatched in a high water and has been told so by everybody who knows her.
appearance.build: Long-legged and broad through the hips, with a prehensile tail-prop she uses to unload weight and a brood pouch that shows on her as a slack across the lower belly when it is empty. Her stance is three points: two splayed feet and the tail, and it never settles onto a heel, which is the shape of her and the reason for everything else about how she stands.
appearance.complexion: Grey-green and slick, drying to a pale matte at the wrists and throat within an hour out of the water, which she treats as an inconvenience rather than as a danger and which is a misjudgement her species has been making for a very long time.
appearance.hair: Fine, dark, and worn in a single heavy rope that she ties off above the nape so it stays out of the water. It is soaked through within a minute and she has never once dried it.
appearance.eyes: Large, laterally set and lidless at the brow, which is not decoration: pressure through the feet and the taste of silt are how her species carries the world, and the eyes are the third sense rather than the first. She watches faces badly and surfaces superbly.
appearance.palette: Silt grey-green and wet slate with one warm value, the ochre of a cut bank, which is the only colour on a floodplain and therefore the only colour on her. Her skin is drawn with a wet sheen above the knee and a drying matte below it, and that division is the visual statement of a body whose whole economy is where the water is.
appearance.attire: A short oiled wrap above the knee to keep the sun and the surveyor's eyes off her, and nothing else; marshfolk do not dress for dry ground because there is none of it. The wrap is the only garment in the setting she owns that has ever needed to be taken off, and she takes it off in front of people without any particular self-consciousness about it.
appearance.marks: Silt pressed into the fine wrinkles at her elbow and knee where it dries and stays, and a pale band around each ankle where a float-line has rubbed for eleven seasons. Both are the marks of a body whose skin desiccates fast out of water and which has therefore spent every one of its first thirty-one years within reach of it.
appearance.bearing: Constantly in motion and never fidgeting: she shifts between her three points the way another body shifts weight, and a still photograph of her reads as poised because the pose is a transition. She cannot stand still and has stopped apologising for it to about the fourth person who asked.

canon.role_in_story: The mind path is, in every office and school in this setting, a discipline of sitting. Clear Mind is a daily sitting. Still Point is a discipline of holding the qi still at the moment of release. The whole ladder is priced in what a body can hold perfectly still while a charge is held and then let go, and a marshfolk cannot stand still, because the three-point stance over splayed toes and a tail-prop never loads a heel. Erith Ambrose is the only marshfolk on the Widow Run who has taken the path at all, and she took it in the water, and she has had to invent every posture the discipline requires because the postures it is taught in are not available to her body. She is also a sworn member of a sect whose entire content is that it recognises nothing, so the setting's only mind-path practitioner whose advancement nobody can certify is a marshfolk sitting in a flood.
canon.first_appearance: First seen knee-deep in a channel off the Widow Run with one hand flat on the surface and her weight forward onto the front foot, emptying her head in the middle of a conversation and answering the last question about a quarter of a second before she appeared to have heard the first one.
canon.lore:
A marshfolk is a wading amphibian lineage that breathes air and nests on floating mats, so it is neither a tidecaller nor a Commonborn but the body in between. It exists to occupy ground that is water half the time and land the other half, and it is built for that band and for nothing else.

The anatomy is the whole of it. Long legs with a splayed three-point foot and a prehensile tail-prop, no heel and no structure in its place. That is why the fourteenth gate is the ceiling for the whole species: ordinal fourteen is the first gate that requires both heel vessels simultaneously, and this stance never loads a heel, so qi never pools there. They walk fine. They cannot stand still, and neither has any marshfolk in the record.

The soul is seated low. Qi pools in a broad pelvic basin rather than a compact chest seat, which is why they take qi out of wet ground efficiently and out of dry ground poorly, and it is why the floodplain is not a place they live near. It is the place they can be supplied.

And the senses are the supply. Pressure through the feet and the taste of silt carry the world to them; they feel a vibration through standing water long before they see its source. Those are not two gifts listed beside a cost. They are the same apparatus. The body reads the water and the body drinks it out of the water, and both halves are why a marshfolk on dry ground is slow, poor, and eventually unwell.

So consider what the mind path asks of a body. The whole of it is a sitting. Clear Mind is a daily sitting that empties the head before the day starts, and it is the cheapest passive in the codex and the one thing every tradition asks for first. Still Point holds the qi still at the moment of release, and every technique casts cheaper for it, which is the one property that compounds at mastery. Nine gates of a ladder priced in what a body can hold perfectly, completely, unmoving, and then let go at exactly the right count.

A marshfolk cannot hold still. Not badly and not for short periods: a three-point stance over splayed toes and a tail-prop distributes weight so that no heel ever takes a full load, and that is not a habit. There is nothing in the frame to hold still with. She has never in her life been able to stand in one place for the length of a sitting and she cannot teach herself to, because there is no muscle in the arrangement that would allow it.

So she does it in three points, knee-deep, with one hand flat on the water and her weight forward onto the front foot. She developed it at nineteen out of pure refusal, after being told for two years by people who meant well that a marshfolk might as well not start. The variation she actually uses is not the sitting at all: it is a slow shift of weight through three supports, timed, with the release at the bottom of the shift, where the body is momentarily still because it is between two positions. It works. It is not what the discipline is taught as. It is hers, and there is nobody on the Widow Run, or on the Spirit Peaks, who can say whether it counts.

And then there is the gate. Spirit Transformation is the mind ladder's version of the point at which perception stops being tied to the senses that the physical law supplies. The capacity goes up, the eight meridians of the second group open, and the sharpness becomes measurable rather than claimed. On any other body it is a difficulty of will. On hers it is a severance of the only thing that feeds her, because her senses are her supply: pressure through the feet and taste of silt are how her body finds the qi, and the gate is the gate at which a mind practitioner stops needing the world to tell it anything.

She is two gates below it and she has thought about little else for four years. The trial is sited on the worked face in the Spirit Peaks, which is the driest ground in the setting, because what is projected has to land on something real and because a reservation wide enough to hold a failure belongs on a quarry floor rather than on a ridge. To sit that gate she has to leave standing water for long enough to walk to stone and sit still on it, and her species' skin desiccates fast out of water and long dry seasons kill the young first. Nobody has suggested she is doing this for a reason.

And nobody can record it. She is sworn to a sect whose entire content is that it recognises nothing at all, because recognition begins where office begins and she holds no office. So the setting's one marshfolk mind practitioner has no institution that will certify a gate, no register on which her advancement appears, and no second practitioner of any species on the run who has taken the path to argue with her about whether her variation counts.

The pairing is anatomical and it is tight. Her low, broad basin takes qi out of wet ground efficiently and out of dry ground poorly, and the same pressure through the feet and taste of silt that tells her where the qi is are the senses the path's own method asks her to stop needing. So the whole of her advantage is that she can read the world from inside it, and the gate she is trying to pass is the gate at which a mind practitioner stops reading the world and starts supplying it. She is trying to take the one gate that would make her independent of the exact thing that has kept her alive.

What she wants is for somebody to come and watch her do it and say whether it counts. That is all she has asked for, twice, in writing, to two offices, and she has been told both times that there is no register for a variation nobody else has practised and no fee for certifying one. What she has not said is that she has begun to wonder whether she is going to the worked face to sit the gate or to find out how long she can stay on dry stone at all.
history: Sworn to the sect at sixteen because it is the door that recognises nothing and therefore costs nothing to be inside, and she has held no office since, which means nine years in which nothing she did was written down by anybody.

Began the daily sitting at nineteen in a room, on a reed mat, in the ordinary posture, and discovered inside about four minutes that she could not hold still in it. She has never found anybody since who was surprised by that.

Worked out the three-point variation the following winter, alone, by counting the shift rather than the stillness, and has practised it every day since without once being asked to and without ever having it recognised.

Cleared the ninth gate in a channel at twenty-six with two households watching and neither of them able to say afterwards what they had seen, and has carried the figure since without any office willing to certify it.

Asked twice, in writing, for somebody to come and watch her practise and rule on whether her variation counts, and been told twice that there is no register for it and no fee for certifying it. Has started walking out toward the worked face in the Spirit Peaks and back.

Holding the qi still at the moment of release, which every technique casts cheaper for and which is the one property that compounds at mastery. The Spirit Transformation opening of the mind ladder, sited on the worked face in the Spirit Peaks, where what is projected has to land on something real and where a reservation wide enough to hold a failure belongs on a quarry floor rather than a ridge. It is the driest ground in the setting, it is nine days of hard walking from the Widow Run, and her species' skin desiccates fast out of water. She has started walking toward it and back and has not told anyone what she is measuring.

It needs standing shallow water and it will not take on a bank, so it is a fact about the floodplain that reads as a fact about her: the plant that a marshfolk can harvest is the one plant that cannot be grown anywhere she is ever asked to go. She has cut it since she was old enough to wade and has never once been able to explain to a land-cultivator why it matters which side of a bank it is on.

has nine cleared gates that no office will certify, because there is no register for a variant nobody else has practised and no fee for certifying one
combat_read: She will not close and she is already standing in the only place on the ground where her supply works. Everything that comes at her crosses water first and she feels it in her feet before her eyes have anything to say, which means she begins the engagement before it starts. The pressure that works on her is the bank: get her onto dry ground, even briefly, and her qi draw collapses and her senses go flat at the same moment, because they are one apparatus. Do not try to hold her in the water by force, she weighs almost nothing and she will not stop moving. Make her choose, and she will choose the water every time, and choosing is the only thing that costs her anything.
notes: The advantage and its cost are the same anatomy. Qi pools low and wide in a broad pelvic basin and is drawn efficiently out of wet ground, and the pressure through the feet and taste of silt that locate it are the same senses the mind path's method asks a practitioner to stop needing. Both halves are the marshfolk record as authored; no rule has been invented here to make the pairing land.

Her ninth gate is a real figure and her species' wall at the fourteenth is anatomical: the paired heel vessels cannot form on a three-point stance that never loads a heel. The ordinals are stated rather than approximated.

The three-point variation of the sitting is written as her practice and its habit, not as a technique. The bible does not contain it and nothing here grants her a mechanic for it; it is an untested improvisation with a cost she pays every day.

art.palette_notes: Silt grey-green and wet slate carry the figure, with the single warm value being the ochre of a cut bank and that value appearing only where she is standing near one. The wet sheen above the knee and the drying matte below it is drawn in every shot and is not a lighting note: it is the character. The tail-prop is load-bearing and always in contact with something, and the rope of soaked hair is drawn heavy and tied off. The pale float-line bands at both ankles are visible in close framings only. In every shot she is in one of three positions, and no shot shows her standing on two.
